§1 What this covers

This document gives allowable damage limits for the section 43 wing-to-body fairing skin panels — the panels that fair over the join between fuselage section 43 and the wing root.

Limits only apply if the damage is sealed per Paragraph 2. Otherwise it becomes a repair.

§ Damage definitions

◇ Nick / Gouge / Scratch
◇ Dent damage
Tip — pre-inspection Boeing recommends instrumented NDT for honeycomb damage. Tap test is an acceptable alternative for honeycomb core areas only. Refer 737 NDT Part 1, 51-01-02.

§4.A GFRP Honeycomb — Full Depth Core Area

Pick a panel to see its damage size + spacing diagram with current numbers
◇ Damage size + spacing limits

Understanding the formulas

Plain English D = diameter of the larger damage. d = diameter of the smaller damage. A = min gap required between two damage centers. B = min distance from larger damage to any fastener/edge. C = min distance from smaller damage to any fastener/edge.

What's allowed in Full Depth Core

Cracks

  • Max one facesheet + core deep
  • Size within Table 102 for the panel
  • Spacing per Table 102
  • Sealed per §2

Nicks / Gouges / Scratches

  • That don't damage glass fibers — permitted unconditionally
  • That do damage fibers — within Table 102 + min spacing + sealed

Dents

  • Within Table 102 dimension limit
  • Min distance from fasteners / edges / other damage
  • Sealed per §2

Holes / Punctures

  • Max one facesheet + core deep
  • Within Table 102 dimension
  • Spacing per Table 102
  • Sealed per §2

Delaminations

  • Use larger of visual diameter or NDT-detected diameter
  • Within Table 102 dimension + spacing
  • Sealed per §2

None of the above?

  • It's not allowable damage — refer to the applicable Repair section of the SRM
  • Apply a temporary seal and record the location

§4.B GFRP Honeycomb — Edgeband Area

Note Edgeband limits are tighter and uniform across all panels — no Table 102 lookup needed. Dents are NOT permitted in the edgeband.

DentsNOT PERMITTED——

Worked examples — edgeband

✓ Within limits
"Found a 0.18" hairline crack near the edge"
Crack length 0.18" < 0.25" max · located 0.75" from fastener (need 0.5") · nearest other damage 5.2" away (need 3.0").

→ Seal per §2 and document.
✗ Exceeds limits
"Small dent on the edgeband"
No size matters here — dents are NOT permitted in edgeband zones, period.

→ This becomes a repair under the relevant SRM repair section, not allowable damage.
✓ Within limits
"0.6" delamination at edge"
Delamination 0.6" < 1.0" max · 0.55" from edge (need 0.5") · no other damage within 3.0".

→ Seal per §2.

§4.C Formed Aluminum Sheet Panels

◇ Aluminum damage removal — typical taper geometry

Cracks · Nicks · Gouges · Scratches · Corrosion

  • Remove damaged material to 1.00" min radius
  • Depth X = max 0.10T (T = panel thickness)
  • Taper out at 20X minimum each direction
  • Distance from any edge/fastener/other damage = ≥ 20X
  • Smooth — no sharp creases

Dents

  • Depth Y = max 0.25" (6.4 mm)
  • W/Y ratio = 30 or more (a 0.25" deep dent needs 7.5" width)
  • Smooth — no creases / gouges / cracks
  • No pulled or loose fasteners in dent
  • Min 3.0D from other damage, holes, edges

Holes / Punctures

  • Max 0.25" (6.4 mm) across largest dimension
  • Min 1.0" (25.4 mm) from fastener, edge, or other damage
  • Fill with 2017-T3 or 2117-T4 flush head rivet — no sealant

Corrosion around fasteners

  • Remove fasteners first, then the corroded material
  • Depth removal X = max 0.10T
  • 0.50" min radius around each affected fastener hole
  • Group limit: up to 3 adjacent fasteners in any group of 10
  • Install same-type fastener (up to first oversize) on reassembly

Worked examples — aluminum

✓ Within limits
"0.20" deep dent, 8" long on a 0.040" panel"
Depth Y = 0.20" < 0.25" max
W/Y = 8 / 0.20 = 40 (need ≥30)
Distance to nearest fastener: 4.5" > 3.0×0.20 = 0.6" required

→ Verify smoothness, no creases. Seal per §2.
✗ Exceeds limits
"0.10" deep dent, only 2.5" long"
Depth = 0.10" OK
W/Y = 2.5 / 0.10 = 25 < 30 required

→ Dent is too sharp (sharp creases not allowed). This is not allowable damage — initiate repair.
✓ Within limits
"0.18" puncture from FOD strike, 1.4" from nearest rivet"
Hole Ø = 0.18" < 0.25" max
Distance to fastener: 1.4" > 1.0" required

→ Fill with 2017-T3 or 2117-T4 flush head rivet (no sealant in the hole itself). Then chem conv + BMS 10-11 Type I primer on bare surface.
✓ Within limits
"Surface scratch 1.5" long on a 0.063" panel"
Depth = 0.005" measured = max X allowed: 0.10 × 0.063 = 0.0063" max
Required taper = 20 × 0.005 = 0.1" each side
Remove the scratch to 1.00" min radius, taper out 0.1" minimum. Treatment per §2.B.

Post-removal treatment (aluminum)

  1. Chemical conversion coating on all bare aluminum→ 51-20-01
  2. BMS 10-11 Type I primer, one layer→ SOPM 20-41-02
  3. Verify aerodynamic smoothness — non-compliance hits aircraft performance→ 51-10-01

Reading the table A = 1.7 × (D+d) means the gap between two adjacent damage centers must be at least 1.7 times the sum of their diameters. B = 2.0D means damage center must sit at least 2.0 × its own diameter from any fastener hole or panel edge.

§2 Sealing — GFRP Panels (no aluminum mesh)

Damage one ply deep or less

Temporary seal

interim
  1. Apply aluminum foil tape (speed tape)
  2. Record the location
  3. Check tape at normal maintenance intervals

Permanent seal

final
  1. BMS 8-201 / 8-207 / 8-301 epoxy resin to the area→ 51-70-08
  2. BMS 10-79 Type 3 or BMS 10-103 Type 1 primer, one layer→ SOPM 20-44-04
  3. BMS 10-60 enamel, one layer over the resin→ AMM 51-21-99/701

Damage more than one ply deep

  1. Use vacuum + heat to remove moisture from solid laminate or honeycomb cells→ 51-70-04
  2. Temporary seal with aluminum foil tape
  3. Record the location
  4. Repair within 24 months of the seal date — hard limit

§2.A.3 Sealing — GFRP Panels WITH BMS 8-336 Aluminum Mesh

Different procedure Some panels have expanded aluminum foil mesh for lightning protection. When the mesh itself is damaged, sealing follows a different reference.
  1. Damage limits for the mesh come from 51-70-14 — not this section
  2. Seal the damaged mesh area per 51-70-14

§2.B Sealing — Formed Aluminum Sheet

  1. Remove damaged material per 51-10-02
  2. Apply chemical conversion coating on bare surfaces→ 51-20-01
  3. Apply BMS 10-11 Type I primer, one layer→ SOPM 20-41-02
  4. Confirm aerodynamic smoothness→ 51-10-01
